bullets.title: Raymond James upgrades AMD to Strong Buy, raises PT to $641 on server CPU growth
bullets.body: Raymond James upgraded AMD from Outperform to Strong Buy and raised its price target from $565 to $641, citing the server CPU market expected to reach $201B by 2030 at a 44% five-year CAGR. The upgrade reflects confidence in AMD's positioning in the AI infrastructure buildout.

bullets.title: Raymond James raises NVDA PT to $352, sees CPU business reaching 5% of revenue by 2028
bullets.body: Raymond James raised its NVIDIA price target from $330 to $352, maintaining Strong Buy, with the firm highlighting NVIDIA's accelerating CPU business as a potentially meaningful revenue contributor (~5% by 2028). Markets rallied pre-open with NVDA earnings anticipated as a key catalyst.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: AMD's 2027 agentic AI CPU ramp to foreshadow NVDA CoWoS packaging surge
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees AMD's agentic AI CPU demand ramp in 2027 as a leading indicator of NVIDIA's CoWoS chip packaging demand trajectory, implying strong structural AI chip packaging demand ahead for both names.

bullets.title: Tech sector sees largest de-grossing in two years; NDX at 100-day MA
bullets.body: The tech sector is experiencing its biggest deleveraging in two years with NDX testing its 100-day moving average, even as earnings estimates continue to be revised higher. The divergence between positioning and fundamentals could set up a technical inflection point around NVDA earnings.

bullets.title: AVGO flagged as bearish trend; one of three stocks driving 25% of Monday's SPY decline
bullets.body: Hedgeye notes AVGO and two other stocks accounted for a quarter of Monday's SPY decline, with AVGO characterized as showing a bearish trend. 8 of 11 sectors actually advanced on the down day, suggesting idiosyncratic large-cap drag rather than broad weakness.

bullets.title: NVDA pre-earnings: equities rally, chip stocks rebound on AI optimism
bullets.body: U.S. equities rose pre-market with chip stocks rebounding on AI sentiment ahead of NVDA earnings, July PCE data, and Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole speech. Stubbornly high long-dated Treasury yields and sticky inflation remain headwinds in the backdrop.

bullets.title: Tesla hikes Cybertruck prices by $5,000 amid demand concerns and recalls
bullets.body: Tesla raised U.S. Cybertruck prices by $5,000 across variants: the Dual Motor AWD moves to $74,990 and the all-wheel-drive to $84,990. The price hike comes amid ongoing demand concerns and a backdrop of multiple Cybertruck recalls.

bullets.title: Tim Cook has less than one week left as Apple CEO
bullets.body: According to a tweet flagged in the digest window, Tim Cook officially has fewer than seven days remaining as Apple's CEO, marking an imminent leadership transition at one of the world's largest companies.

bullets.title: Bessent bond buyback gambit vs. Druckenmiller: Treasury short squeeze debate
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent's expanded bond buyback program is framed as a potential catalyst for a Treasury short squeeze — with 30-year yields at 5.34% and CTA funds heavily short — that could drive yields sharply lower. Druckenmiller publicly criticized the intervention, arguing rising borrowing costs reflect deeper structural problems that buybacks won't fix.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole expected to trigger outsized market moves; Fed Chair Warsh speech in focus
bullets.body: This year's Jackson Hole symposium is seen as a potential catalyst for significant market volatility with investors parsing Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's remarks closely. July's Fed communication was characterized as providing little policy clarity, heightening sensitivity to any new signals.

bullets.title: US sanctions over 60 Iran-linked entities ('Operation Economic Outcast'); China spared
bullets.body: The U.S. launched 'Operation Economic Outcast,' sanctioning 60+ entities tied to Iran's oil, nuclear, and missile activities, while deliberately sparing major Chinese banks despite China purchasing over 80% of Iranian oil. China warned of potential retaliation per FT, though a US-China AI and trade cooperation agreement was separately announced via Xinhua.

bullets.title: ETF flows: Government Bond ETFs see largest inflows; US Large Cap ETFs post largest outflows
bullets.body: For the week ended 8/21/26, Government Bond ETFs recorded the largest inflows across all categories, while U.S. Large Cap ETFs saw the largest outflows after turning negative — consistent with a rotation out of equities into fixed income amid elevated yields.

bullets.title: Wolfe Research: August payrolls to beat consensus at 65K; unemployment edging to 4.16%
bullets.body: Wolfe Research forecasts 65,000 jobs added in August versus the 55,000 consensus, with private payrolls adding 75,000 offset by a 10,000 decline in government payrolls. Unemployment is projected to tick up slightly to 4.16%.

bullets.title: China data center electricity demand to 4x by 2030, exceeding South Korea's current total
bullets.body: China's data centers are projected to quadruple their electricity usage by 2030, surpassing South Korea's entire current power consumption — a structural demand signal for AI infrastructure and power supply chains.

bullets.title: UBS warns uranium market is 'structurally tightening'; sector awakens after 5-month slumber
bullets.body: UBS issued a note flagging structural tightening in the uranium market after a five-month dormancy period, with supply-demand dynamics improving for producers including UEC.

bullets.title: AAOI turning away CPO laser customers; photonics co-dev visibility key for SIVE earnings
bullets.body: Ahead of SIVE earnings in two days, a trader highlights that AAOI disclosed it had to turn away multiple customers approaching them for CPO lasers — flagging strong demand signals in the photonic co-packaging space as a key indicator to watch.

bullets.title: COPX outperforming NVDA sharply YTD; copper seen as real AI infrastructure play
bullets.body: Copper ETF COPX is up 33% YTD vs. NVDA's +12%, and up 55% since October while NVDA is flat over the same period. The framing challenges the semiconductor-centric AI narrative and points to copper/materials as the more tangible AI infrastructure beneficiary.

bullets.title: Chicago Fed National Activity Index dips to -0.08 in July; job-seeking intentions rebounding
bullets.body: The Chicago Fed's July CFNAI fell to -0.08 from +0.06 in June with only 40 of 85 indicators positive, signaling below-trend economic activity. Separately, NY Fed data shows job-seeking intentions rebounded to 24.9% in July from 22.5% in March, with the biggest gains among workers earning under $60K.

bullets.title: US July building permits revised down to 1.433M annual rate; monthly growth cut to +4.3%
bullets.body: US July building permits were revised down to a 1.433M annual rate from the initial 1.443M, with monthly growth adjusted lower to +4.3% from +5.0% — a modest but directionally negative revision for housing supply.

bullets.title: Market breadth positive despite index weakness; volume decelerating on down days
bullets.body: Despite Monday's SPY decline, 8 of 11 sectors advanced, and volume continues to decelerate on down days in August — technical signals that Hedgeye characterizes as consistent with broadening into what they call 'Quad 1,' with SPY remaining in an 'investable' volatility bucket.
